subtopics.title: What Counts as Non-conventional, and Why South Africa Is Blessed

questions.question: The two defining properties of non-conventional energy sources are:
options: The fuel is free — sunshine and wind arrive without mining or importing — but the flows are intermittent, needing storage, backup or a smart mix
They are expensive to fuel but steady to run
They require imported fuel and produce no waste
They work only at small household scale

questions.question: The evidence for South Africa's exceptional solar endowment is:
options: Rainfall above 1 000 millimetres over the interior
More than 2 500 sunshine hours per year over most of the interior, with the Northern Cape among the world's premium solar territories
The country's position on the equator
Cloud cover equal to Germany's

questions.question: The REIPPPP is:
options: A carbon tax on coal exports
Eskom's maintenance programme
The competitive bidding programme under which private developers build wind and solar farms and sell power to the grid on long contracts
A rooftop solar subsidy for households

questions.question: The 'quiet economic reversal' behind this topic is that:
options: Coal became free to mine
Electricity demand stopped growing
Nuclear became the cheapest source
REIPPPP auctions drove prices down until new wind and solar became cheaper per kilowatt-hour than new coal

subtopics.title: Solar Energy: South African and World Examples

questions.question: The core difference between PV and CSP is:
options: PV converts sunlight directly to electricity in semiconductor cells with no moving parts, while CSP focuses mirrors to heat a fluid and drive a steam turbine
PV works only in deserts while CSP works anywhere
CSP is a household technology and PV is utility-scale only
PV requires water cooling and CSP does not

questions.question: CSP's decisive gift over PV is:
options: Silent operation
Storage — insulated tanks of hot molten salt keep generating steam for hours after sunset, answering intermittency directly
Cheaper panels
Working in cloudy weather

questions.question: Redstone, near Postmasburg in the Northern Cape, is notable for:
options: Being Africa's oldest PV farm
Generating from wave power
Being a CSP tower plant with twelve hours of molten-salt storage, built to serve the evening peak
Supplying only mines

questions.question: A world example pairing for solar is:
options: Denmark for CSP and Morocco for offshore panels
Russia dominating panel manufacture
Britain leading desert solar
China dominating panel manufacturing and installed capacity, and Morocco's Noor complex at Ouarzazate as Africa's CSP giant

subtopics.title: Wind Energy: South African and World Examples

questions.question: Wind power rises with the cube of wind speed, which means:
options: Doubling the wind gives eight times the power — why towers reach past a hundred metres into faster, steadier air
Doubling the wind doubles the power
Power falls as wind strengthens
Blade length is irrelevant to output

questions.question: South Africa's leading wind province, with the Jeffreys Bay and Cookhouse farms, is:
options: Gauteng
The Eastern Cape
Limpopo
The Free State

questions.question: Denmark's significance in wind energy is that it:
options: Hosts the world's largest single farm
Invented the cube law
Generates roughly half its electricity from wind and exports its turbine industry — proof a small country can lead a global technology
Banned onshore turbines

questions.question: Wind's honest cost column includes:
options: High fuel prices and water use
Carbon emissions during operation
Ash disposal and acid drainage
Intermittency, visual and noise objections, bird and bat collisions requiring careful siting, and the need for backup in still air

subtopics.title: The Future: Economy, Environment and the Honest Obstacles

questions.question: The economic positives of the renewable build include:
options: Cheapest new power restraining tariffs, hundreds of billions in investment, rural jobs and community revenue in provinces like the Northern Cape, and a green manufacturing ladder
Guaranteed employment for all coal miners
Immediate replacement of all imports
Higher electricity prices funding Eskom

questions.question: The phrase 'just transition' exists because:
options: Renewables need no workers at all
Coal employs about ninety thousand miners concentrated in Mpumalanga towns, and the shift redistributes work across provinces and skills — requiring retraining, pensions and new industry
Transitions must happen within one year
Only lawyers manage energy policy

questions.question: The binding physical constraint on South Africa's renewable pace is now:
options: A shortage of sunshine hours
The unavailability of turbines
The grid — the best sun and wind lie far from Gauteng's demand and the transmission lines are full
A ban on private generation

questions.question: The lesson's defensible conclusion on the non-conventional future is:
options: The resource is too weak to matter
Coal will regain its share by 2040
Storage makes the grid unnecessary
The question is not resource — ours is world-class — but delivery: grid, storage, policy and a just transition; the argument is only about speed

subtopics.title: Fuel That Falls From the Sky

questions.question: The free filling station picture captures:
options: Sunshine and wind costing nothing, with nearly all cost in building the harvesting equipment — paid once, harvesting for decades
Government fuel subsidies
The falling price of petrol
Free electricity for all households

questions.question: 'Free but moody, against costly but steady' summarises:
options: Solar panel maintenance schedules
The trade-off between intermittent renewables and fuel-hungry but steady coal — the whole modern energy argument in five words
The difference between PV and CSP
Wind farm rental agreements

questions.question: Germany's relevance to South Africa's solar debate is that it:
options: Has better sun than the Northern Cape
Abandoned solar as unworkable
Built a world-leading solar industry with roughly half our sunshine — proving the race is about pumps, not fuel
Buys most of South Africa's electricity

questions.question: The PV panel's one-line secret is:
options: Sunlight to electricity with no moving parts — silent, strongest at noon, asleep by dusk
Mirrors focused on a tower
Steam driving a turbine
Heat stored in molten salt

questions.question: CSP's 'thermos' superpower means:
options: The mirrors stay warm overnight
Hot molten salt stored in insulated tanks keeps making steam for hours — supper-time electricity from lunchtime sun
The plant needs no sunlight at all
Panels are insulated against frost

questions.question: Wind turbines and farming coexist because:
options: Turbines fertilise the soil
Farms are always abandoned before construction
Sheep graze under the turbines while farmers collect rent and communities hold revenue shares
Turbines are built only on barren rock

questions.question: The correct place pairings are:
options: Jeffreys Bay CSP; Upington wind
Redstone in Gauteng; Cookhouse in Limpopo
Noor in Denmark; Caledon in China
PV mega-farms around Upington and De Aar; CSP at Khi, KaXu, Xina and Redstone in the Northern Cape; wind at Jeffreys Bay, Cookhouse and Caledon on the coastal belt

subtopics.title: The Relay Race and the Baton

questions.question: Fumble one — 'the extension cord' — refers to:
options: Full transmission lines between the Northern and Eastern Cape's resources and Gauteng's demand, making new lines the real bottleneck
Households using unsafe wiring
The cost of undersea cables to Europe
Solar panels needing longer cables than coal

questions.question: The 'night shift' is covered by:
options: Running coal stations harder at night forever
A designed mix — CSP's hot salt, batteries, pumped storage, and coastal wind that often blows while solar sleeps
Importing electricity from Germany
Switching demand off at sunset

questions.question: Passing the baton 'justly' means:
options: Closing all mines immediately
Letting the market decide alone
Retraining, pensions, new industry and international transition finance for coal towns like Emalahleni and Secunda
Delaying renewables until 2050

questions.question: The finish-line verdict on the non-conventional future is:
options: Direction uncertain, speed certain
Both direction and speed are unknowable
The environment loses under any scenario
The direction is not in doubt — sun and wind win on environment and increasingly on economics — only the speed is argued, and it depends on wires, storage and justice
